thread:
Noah Patel: heads up / coordination request w/ releases. we’ve got a couple “risky” runtime changes landing this week (scheduler heuristics + kernel auto-select tweak) and i really want to avoid stacking them in the same merge window / rollout. can we align on a merge freeze + rollout order for 0.28.7?

Noah Patel: context: perf-canary is still tuning thresholds in us-east, and we’re using it as the primary gate for runtime rollouts. if we land both scheduler + kernel changes in the same train, any p95 regression is gonna be impossible to attribute quickly.

Connor O'Brien: :eyes: yep. what’s the current list of changes you consider “risky”? trying to map to the release calendar.

Noah Patel: risky items (from our side):
- scheduler: new batching depth heuristic (Sofia’s) (behind flag but default-on in canary env)
- kernels: updated flash-attn kernel selection for long prefill buckets (Hiro’s) (also behind flag)
- instrumentation: queueing time metric + kernel tag propagation (Omar) (should be safe-ish but touches hot path)

Noah Patel: non-risky that i’m ok to batch: logging redaction asserts + canary auth scope updates.

Sofia Ivanova: +1 on separating scheduler from kernels. the heuristic changes queueing/batch formation; if kernel selection shifts too, it’ll be a mess to tell if it’s compute vs queue.

Hiro Tanaka: agree. kernel tweak is mostly for long prompts (prefill heavy). in isolation we can validate w/ canary prompt buckets pretty cleanly.

Connor O'Brien: ok. release train wise we were targeting:
- merge window closes Wed 18:00 PT
- cut candidate Thu AM
- rollout Fri (us-east first) w/ canary gates

Connor O'Brien: but we can adjust if needed. what do you want the order to be?

Noah Patel: proposal:
1) this train (0.28.7): land instrumentation + tagging + canary gate wiring only (queueing time, kernel version tags). keep scheduler/kernels flags OFF by default.
2) next train (0.28.8): scheduler heuristic ON (kernel flag stays OFF).
3) following train: kernel auto-select change ON.

Noah Patel: that gives us clean attribution windows and avoids “double-risk” in a single rollout.

Vanessa Ortiz: fyi infra has a GPU driver patch slated for Fri night in eu-west dedicated pool. doesn’t affect us-east hosted, but if you’re planning eu-west expansion soon, might want to avoid same day.

Noah Patel: good catch. we were talking about expanding canary coverage to eu-west next week (not this Fri). we can keep eu-west rollout paused until after driver patch stabilizes.

Connor O'Brien: from releases POV: easiest is to enforce a “one risky perf change per train” rule for runtime. can you define what’s risky in release notes and in the gating checklist? i can add it to the rollout checklist doc.

Noah Patel: yes. i’ll update the checklist + add a note to ENG-4872 umbrella.

Omar El-Sayed: instrumentation changes: queueing time metric export is already in review, but it is on hot path. it should be very low overhead (just reading existing timestamps) and behind sampling. i can also put it behind `RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_QUEUE_METRIC=on` if you want extra safety.

Rafael Mendes: from oncall side: pls avoid Friday afternoon surprises :)) if we’re enabling paging phase-1 soon, i’d prefer the first “risky default-on” happens Mon-Thu PT.

Connor O'Brien: +1. we can still cut on Thu, but any flag flips / default-on should be early week.

Sofia Ivanova: works for me. my heuristic is already behind `sched_batch_v2` flag. i can keep default-off for 0.28.7 and only enable in canary namespace first.

Hiro Tanaka: kernel change: same. behind `kernel_autoselect_v4`. we can do: enable in canary (us-east) -> observe 24h -> enable 10% dedicated -> then hosted.

Noah Patel: perfect. for this week’s merge window:
- ok to merge instrumentation/tagging + guardrails
- do NOT merge any flag-default flips (scheduler/kernels) into 0.28.7

Noah Patel: Connor can you confirm we can “branch protect” 0.28.7 after Wed 18:00 and punt any late perf changes to 0.28.8?

Connor O'Brien: yes. i’ll mark 0.28.7 as “stabilization only” after Wed 18:00 PT. any perf-affecting diffs after that need explicit approval + runtime+SRE signoff.

Vanessa Ortiz: also please tag driver patch in the rollout notes so when canary yells we don’t chase ghosts.

Noah Patel: yep, will add a “fleet events” section to the rollout doc (region/SKU).

Mateo Alvarez: jumping in late — +1 to the stagger. our goal with canary is fast RCA; stacking scheduler+kernels defeats that. Connor, thanks for making the process change.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: action items:
- Noah: update release checklist w/ “one risky perf change per train” + define risky
- Omar: confirm metrics overhead + add optional env toggle if trivial
- Sofia/Hiro: keep default flips out of 0.28.7, schedule flag enablement early next week w/ canary gate

Noah Patel: ack. i’ll post a short summary in #eng-releases too w/ proposed order + timing.

Rafael Mendes: pls also link the canary dashboard and runbook in that summary. oncall will thank you.

Noah Patel: will do. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/perf-canary (internal) runbook: https://confluence.redwood.example/runbooks/perf-canary-alert (internal)

Connor O'Brien: cool. locking this in for 0.28.7. ping me if anything changes / urgent.

Hiro Tanaka: :thumbsup:

Sofia Ivanova: :thumbsup:

Omar El-Sayed: will add the env toggle + note in PR description.

Noah Patel: thanks all. (and yes, no Friday flag flips :pray:)
